name: Dynamic Epsilon for Self-Intersection Prevention
definition: A method to prevent self-intersections of secondary rays (e.g., refraction) by computing a local offset epsilon dynamically at each intersection point, rather than using a global epsilon value. This is necessary because sphere tracing intersection distances vary significantly, making global epsilon inappropriate for screen-space metrics.
summary: Dynamic epsilon prevents self-intersection in sphere tracing by computing a local offset that adapts to surface distance, solving issues with global constants under screen-space termination.
